title: Training and canopy
subtitle: Shaping the vine
objectives: Compare bush vines and trellised systems

steps.title: Training systems
steps.body: Bush vines, or gobelet, stand alone without wires, shading their fruit; they suit hot, dry, windy places like southern Spain or Barossa's old vineyards. Trellised systems hold shoots along wires, giving even sun exposure and making mechanisation possible. Vertical shoot positioning, or VSP, is the most common trellis in cool regions.
steps.highlight: Bush in heat; trellis for control

steps.title: Pruning
steps.body: In winter, growers prune to decide how many buds, and so how many bunches, each vine carries. Cane pruning leaves one or two long canes of last year's wood, each with 8 to 15 buds; common in Bordeaux and New Zealand. Spur pruning leaves short spurs of 2 or 3 buds along a permanent arm, called a cordon; easier to mechanise.
steps.highlight: Canes are long; spurs are short

steps.prompt: Why are bush vines common in hot, dry regions?
options: Their leaves shade the fruit and they need no wires
They are easy to machine harvest
steps.explanation: The open, low shape shades the grapes from harsh sun and suits poor, dry soils without the cost of trellising.

steps.title: Canopy decisions
steps.body: Canopy management balances leaves and fruit. About 1 to 1.5 m2 of leaf area per kilo of fruit ripens it well. In cool, damp places, growers remove leaves around bunches for sun and airflow. In hot ones, they keep leaves to prevent sunburn, or use shade netting. Hedging, topping and shoot thinning fine-tune the canopy.
steps.highlight: Enough leaves to ripen, enough air to stay healthy

steps.prompt: In very hot regions, growers often remove all leaves around the bunches to maximise sunlight.
steps.explanation: Not true. In hot regions, exposed bunches can sunburn. Growers usually keep leaves for shade; leaf removal is more common in cool, damp places.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Bush vines suit heat and drought; trellises give control
Cane pruning keeps long canes; spur pruning short spurs
Canopy management balances sunlight, airflow and ripening
